reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Local authority for contract or day-labor road work
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8595), cross-references (64.050, 64.080, 231.340, 231.350), and case annotations (Polk Twp., Miller). Covers county commission, township board, and road district commissioner authority when expending tax or bond funds on roads, bridges, or culverts by contract or by day labor with machinery, materials, and hired help.

headings.title: Accepting donated labor or materials and completing work
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers permissive authority of county commissions, township boards, and road district commissioners to accept labor or material donations from interested parties for road improvements or bridge construction and hire labor or contractors to finish the work.

headings.title: Pre-construction filing and approval of plans and estimates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. Covers mandatory filing of plans, specifications, drainage estimates, maps, profiles, cost estimates, and specific location with the county clerk, township clerk, or road district commissioner and local authority approval before starting contract or day-labor work.

headings.title: Cost statements, account payments, and engineer supervision
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and section notes. Covers post-completion cost statement filing under section 229.050 and recording in the bids book, review and payment of engineer-certified payrolls and construction accounts, and required supervision by the county highway engineer or another employed competent engineer paid from the project fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8595), cross-references (64.050, 64.080, 231.340, 231.350), and annotations (Polk Twp., Miller), and verified all fingerprints. Checked county/township/road-district contract and day-labor authority, donated labor/materials, pre-construction plan filing/approval, § 229.050 cost statements, certified account payments, and engineer supervision proviso; all four drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Plans and estimates for contracts estimated over $500
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8596). Covers local authorities ordering the county highway engineer or employed engineer(s) to prepare and file maps, plans, specifications, profiles, and cost estimates for contracted road, bridge, or culvert work estimated over $500, and authority to approve or reject them. Independent review revised title from 'Plans and estimates for contracts exceeding $500' because the statutory threshold turns on the engineer's estimated cost exceeding $500.

headings.title: Newspaper advertisement of contract letting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers ordering the engineer, after plan approval, to advertise contract letting in a county newspaper once weekly for three consecutive weeks, with the last insertion within 10 days of letting.

headings.title: Bid submission, public opening, and bidder security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers written sealed bids with engineer instructions and unit prices on road work, public opening/reading/recording, and required 10% certified check or bidder's bond guaranteeing contract and bond execution within 10 days of acceptance notice or 10% forfeiture.

headings.title: Bid rejection, contract award, and attached documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers award to the lowest responsible bidder, county commission discretion to reject any or all bids, mandatory rejection of bids exceeding the engineer's estimate, order of record to contract, and required contract attachments.

headings.title: Contract preservation and terms for work changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers permanent filing of executed approved contracts, reserved local right to alter/omit/substitute work or materials without surety notice, and bidder agreement on prior ordering, written record agreement, and unit-price valuation of changes (retaining exact archived syntax in the final clause without silent alteration).

headings.title: Change-price disputes and labor and material payment terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers binding determination by the state highway engineer when parties disagree on the cost or price of an ordered change (entered of record) and the required contract term obligating the contractor to furnish and promptly pay for all labor and materials.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8596) and verified all fingerprints. Checked the $500 engineer-estimate trigger, three-week newspaper advertising, sealed bidding and 10% security/forfeiture, award/rejection rules, permanent contract filing and change terms (retaining garbled final-clause syntax in subsection 5 without silent repair), and state highway engineer change-price finality plus prompt labor/material payment terms. Revised subsection 1 to 'Plans and estimates for contracts estimated over $500'; retained subsections 2-6.

headings.title: Monthly written work reports by contractors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8598). Covers each road or bridge contractor's duty to submit a detailed written report of the preceding month's work to the engineer in charge on or before the second day of each month.

headings.title: Engineer examination, annotation, and filing of reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers engineer examination of the contractor's report, attaching written errors or explanations for local authorities, certifying correctness when accurate, and filing with the county clerk, township clerk, or district commissioner.

headings.title: Partial contract payments and restriction on full payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers local authority examination of reports and permissive partial contract payments deemed safe and just under the contract, while prohibiting full payment until completion and engineer acceptance.

headings.title: Engineer inspections and sworn statement before final settlement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers periodic engineer inspections and reports plus the prerequisite personal inspection and written statement under oath of contract performance before final settlement with any contractor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8598) and verified all fingerprints. Checked monthly contractor reporting by the second day, engineer examination/annotation/filing, permissive partial payments with bar on full payment before completion/acceptance, and periodic inspections plus sworn personal-inspection statement before final settlement; all four drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Supervision of driveways and ditch crossings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8581, A.L. 2017 S.B. 283). Covers requiring driveways or ditch crossings connecting highways with private property to be made under supervision of the road overseer or road district commissioners.

headings.title: Prohibited willful road and drainage obstructions or damage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the prohibition against willfully and knowingly obstructing or damaging public roads, ditches, or drainage by diverting water, depositing debris, fencing, planting hedges, placing advertising signs within road lines, relocating roads, or other means.

headings.title: Conservation and grading exception for farms and ranches
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2017 S.B. 283). Exempts road damage or obstruction resulting from improving farming or ranching lands via conforming Missouri soil and water conservation program or NRCS technical-standard practices, or precision level grading.

headings.title: Violation notice and court petitions for entry
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note (A.L. 2017 S.B. 283). Covers permissive tracked-mail written notice by the road overseer or county highway engineer to remove/repair/pay, associate circuit court petitions (with cost estimate) after 30 days of noncompliance, required hearing opportunity, and limited non-trespass entry to restore roadways or ditches.

headings.title: Judgments, liens, costs, and attorney's fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note (A.L. 2017 S.B. 283). Covers both outcomes of a subsection 4 petition: if granted, an award of reasonable removal/repair costs, court costs, and reasonable attorney's fees becoming a tax-collected land lien; if denied, county liability for the landowner's court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.

headings.title: Exemption for charter counties and cities not within a county
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note (A.L. 2017 S.B. 283). Preserves the exact body phrasing exempting any county with a charter form of government or any city not within a county (official catchline summarizes this as charter counties and St. Louis City).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections and history/prior revisions (through A.L. 2017 S.B. 283) and verified all fingerprints. Checked ditch-crossing supervision, willful/knowing obstruction prohibitions, farm/ranch conservation and precision-grading exceptions, tracked-mail notice and associate circuit court entry petitions with hearing prerequisite, dual judgment/lien/fee outcomes, and charter-county/city-not-within-a-county exclusion; all six drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Permit applications and required information for moving structures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8600). Covers filing permit applications with the county clerk to move houses, buildings, or structures on public highways outside first-, second-, or third-class or scheme/special-charter cities, and required dimensions, route, utility-line, pole, and railroad-crossing details.

headings.title: Authority to require changes in moving route
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers authority of the county surveyor, highway engineer, or county commission to require route changes deemed proper under attendant circumstances.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8600) and verified all fingerprints. Checked geographic exclusions for first-/second-/third-class and scheme/special-charter cities, required structure/route/wire/railroad application contents, and county surveyor/highway engineer/commission route-change authority; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Owner duty to furnish workers after 229.250 notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8602, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1845). Covers the duty of owners or operators of poles, wires, transmission/feed/trolley lines, or steam/interurban railroads, after section 229.250 notice, to furnish competent workmen or linemen to facilitate moving a structure.

headings.title: Expense payment, federal-height exception, and surety bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by governing costs when owners/operators perform the work: requester pays actual additional expenses (excluding fixed expenses), owner/operator pays if required solely due to federal minimum wire-height noncompliance, and owner/operator may require a payment bond or surety agreement. Notes that the last three sentences are repeated verbatim in subsection 3 of the archived source.

headings.title: Mover interference prohibition, refusal procedures, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by prohibiting structure movers from interfering with poles, wires, or transmission lines unless the owner/operator refuses after section 229.250 notice, requiring competent linemen, careful work, and prompt restoration/repair, and repeating verbatim the actual-additional-expense, federal wire-height noncompliance, and surety-bond sentences from subsection 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior revisions (through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1845) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 229.250 notice triggers, owner/operator duty to furnish workers, mover interference prohibition/refusal procedure, and verified that the final three sentences of subsection 2 (actual additional expenses excluding fixed expenses, federal minimum wire-height noncompliance exception, and surety bond) are repeated verbatim in subsection 3 of the archived source; all three drafted titles retained with clear distinction between subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Engineer route rules, use conditions, and permit refusal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 §§ 8649, 8650, A.L. 1945 p. 1489 § 8649). Covers county highway engineer authority to require route changes, prescribe time/method/manner of moving or public-way use, and refuse an application for good cause to protect rights-of-way or public safety.

headings.title: Cash deposits, restoration bonds, and six-month maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive engineer requirement of cash or bond and mandatory bond conditions to refill/restore disturbed public ways to prior condition, maintain them for six months after completion, and hold the county harmless from related costs during that period.

headings.title: Fiscal-year general bonds for frequent permit applicants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive allowance for applicants whose business or occupation requires frequent special use permits to post a single general bond covering all uses during the county's fiscal year. Independent review revised title from 'Annual general bonds for frequent permit applicants' to match the exact statutory period ('fiscal year of the county').

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior revisions (through A.L. 1945 p. 1489 § 8649) and verified all fingerprints. Checked engineer route/method rules and good-cause permit refusal, permissive cash/bond with restoration, six-month maintenance, and hold-harmless terms, and frequent-applicant general bonds for the county fiscal year. Revised subsection 3 to 'Fiscal-year general bonds for frequent permit applicants'; retained subsections 1-2.

headings.title: Written restoration notice after failure to restore
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8651, A.L. 1945 p. 1489 § 8650). Covers written notice by the county highway engineer and surveyor when an applicant fails or refuses to restore a disturbed public way within 30 days of completion (or a longer written extension), directing restoration, six-month maintenance, and holding the county harmless.

headings.title: County restoration and recovery from deposit or bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive authority of the highway engineer and surveyor, if the applicant fails or refuses to restore within 10 days after receiving a registered notice letter, to have the work done and charge the expense against the cash deposit or by action on the bond.

headings.title: Deposit refunds and preserved penalties under 229.300 to 229.370
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers refunding any remaining cash deposit balance upon fulfilling all obligations and preserving criminal prosecution, conviction, fine, or penalty liability under sections 229.300 to 229.370 notwithstanding deposit deduction or bond recovery.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior revisions (through A.L. 1945 p. 1489 § 8650) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 30-day restoration failure notice and six-month maintenance terms, 10-day post-registered-letter county restoration with deposit/bond recovery, and deposit balance refunds plus preserved criminal penalties under sections 229.300 to 229.370; all three drafted titles retained.

headings.title: County commission approval and prosecuting attorney contract preparation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8862). Covers mandatory submission of a special road district or township board mineral/coal road-removal proposition to the county commission for approval or rejection, and directing the prosecuting attorney to prepare the contract upon approval.

headings.title: Contract contents, rebuilding bond, and temporary road terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers required contract terms (temporarily abandoned road, rebuilt road specifications, time limit) and pre-execution surety bond (at least four times estimated rebuilding cost, payable to the state for the district/township, commission-approved) covering mineral removal, temporary parallel road construction/maintenance if deemed necessary or feasible, negligence liability, timely rebuilding, and optional penalties or liquidated damages.

headings.title: Conditions for acceptance and release of rebuilding bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers bond release only upon completion per plans/contract, county commission acceptance, satisfaction of all bond conditions, and full settlement and discharge of all arising claims, liabilities, and causes of action.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8862) and verified all fingerprints. Checked special road district/township mineral-removal submission to the county commission and prosecuting attorney contract preparation, 4x rebuilding bond and conditional temporary parallel road/negligence terms, and completion/acceptance/claim-discharge conditions for bond release; all three drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Definitions for sections 229.475 to 229.481
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1) to (3)) and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 536 § 1 subsecs. 1, 2). Defines "Commission", "Plants", and "Plant parts" specifically for sections 229.475 to 229.481.

headings.title: Prohibition on unauthorized plant removal and misdemeanor penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers the prohibition on digging or removing plants or plant parts from commission real property or state/county highway or roadway rights-of-way without permission (qualified by section 229.477 and authorized construction/repair/maintenance work), class B misdemeanor penalty, and each plant removed constituting a separate offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections (including subdivisions (1)-(3) of subsection 1) and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 536 § 1 subsecs. 1, 2) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section-range scope (229.475 to 229.481) for definitions, unauthorized plant/plant-part removal prohibition qualified by section 229.477 and authorized maintenance work, class B misdemeanor penalty, and per-plant separate-offense rule; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Exemption for authorized weed and disease control
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 536 § 1 subsecs. 3, 4). Exempts control or eradication of diseased vegetation or noxious weeds by authorized personnel from section 229.475(2).

headings.title: Noncommercial exemption for edibles, seeds, research, and education
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Exempts collection of seeds, fruits, nuts, berries, edible wild greens, or flowering parts, and occasional collection for scientific research or education, from section 229.475(2), strictly conditioned on not offering the plants or plant parts for sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 536 § 1 subsecs. 3, 4) and verified all fingerprints. Checked authorized weed/disease control exemption and noncommercial exemption (not offered for sale) for listed seeds/fruits/nuts/berries/edible wild greens/flowering parts and occasional scientific research or education collection without conflating 'plant parts' defined in section 229.475(1)(3); both drafted titles retained.
